CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: breast

0 of 6 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 3 fall below it; 3 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • myo-inositol: ✗ not detectable

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] glycogen (glycoCEST) — no concentration data found for human breast tissue; chicken breast muscle values (PMID 3816147) are poultry pectoral muscle, not human mammary tissue; [model's own exclusion] glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST) — no evidence found; breast is not a cartilaginous tissue; [model's own exclusion] proteins/peptides as amide pool (APT) — APT imaging shows detectable CEST contrast in breast (PMID 23559550, 34477453) indicating mobile protein/peptide content, but no concentration in mM of amide units was reported; qualitative effect only; [model's own exclusion] glycerophosphocholine (GPC) — reported at ~0.5 μmol/g, below 1 mM threshold; [model's own exclusion] choline — reported at ~0.3 μmol/g, below 1 mM; [model's own exclusion] lactate — qualitatively present but no concentration ≥1 mM found in normal breast tissue; [model's own exclusion] alanine, glutamate, succinate — detected in HR-MAS but concentrations below 1 mM; [model's own exclusion] phosphomonoesters (PME), phosphodiesters (PDE) — 31P spectroscopic groupings, not chemically defined molecules; [model's own exclusion] total choline (tCho) — a spectroscopic sum, not a single molecule; [model's own exclusion] drugs/xenobiotics (tamoxifen, capecitabine, isoflavones) — not endogenous

myo-inositol — CEST: ✗ not detectable

Concentration: 1.20 mM typical (0.5–2.0)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Sitter et al. 2006 reported myo-inositol at ~1.2 μmol/g wet weight in breast tissue, with variation. Converting, ~1.2 mM. The value sits near the 1 mM threshold; some samples may be slightly below. It has 6 exchangeable -OH groups making it a multi-pool CEST target.

Robustness to input uncertainty: no

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (six hydroxyl OH groups [hydroxyl]: concentration 0.5-2 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.01-0.02%, 1.5 T: 0.01-0.04%, 3 T: 0.02-0.09%, 5 T: 0.04-0.17%, 7 T: 0.07-0.26%. Threshold 0.5%.

Frequency-collision analysis: At all field strengths (0.5-7 T), myo-inositol (+0.72 ppm) overlaps with β-glucose hydroxyls (+1.60 ppm): separation 18.6-260.8 Hz vs combined exchange-broadened linewidth ~1058 Hz — pools never resolve. At ≤3 T, also blurs with creatine guanidinium (+2.00 ppm). At 0.5 T, semisolid MT also overlaps. This severely limits specificity in breast where glucose is also present.

Direct water saturation: At 0.5 T (B1=0.1 µT, direct_sat_bandwidth=4.3 Hz), the 0.72 ppm offset ≈ 15.3 Hz is only ~3.5× the bandwidth — the signal is nearly lost in the water saturation tail. At higher fields separation improves (7 T: offset 596 Hz, bandwidth 42.6 Hz), but the exchange regime remains fast at ≤5 T.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex = 600 s⁻¹ and shift 0.725 ppm from human brain in vivo (PMID 20951217) — not breast-specific. Brain pH (~7.2) differs from breast tumor pH (~6.5-7.0); pH affects hydroxyl exchange rates (base-catalyzed). The true kex in breast tumors could be lower (slower exchange at lower pH), potentially reducing contrast further. No breast-specific measurement exists — borrowed from brain.

Potential clinical impact

hydroxyl (CEST, ~1.2-1.4 ppm): 1 CEST/NOE application and 0 metabolite-change studies verified (1 human, 0 animal; 12 humans, 0 animals; 2 dropped by verification). One CEST study (PMID 27100284) detected myo-inositol CEST in breast cancer cell-line extracts, with decreasing CEST signal at higher aggressiveness. HR-MAS MRS confirms myo-inositol in breast cancer tissue correlates with extracellular-matrix biology. CEST evidence at cell level only; metabolite-change in human tissue.

quote
“The highest CEST contrast was generated by creatine, myo-inositol, glutamate, and glycerophosphocholine, whose cellular concentrations decreased with increasing breast cancer aggressiveness.”
full text: “CEST-MRI contrast of the same water-soluble extracts from these breast epithelial and breast cancer cells was measured at physiological pH at 37°C. The average CEST-MRI contrast quantified as MTRasym per cell (n=6 each) at 1.0 ppm, 1.8 ppm, and 3.6 ppm was the highest in MCF-12A, intermediate in MCF-7, and the lowest in MDA-MB-231 cell extracts, indicating that metabolite CEST-MRI can detect metabolite concentration differences resulting from differences in the aggressiveness of the tested water-soluble extracts of breast cancer cell lines.”

Pooled group difference not computed: fewer than 3 verified studies with group means, SDs and sizes for one evidence type and disease category.

Caveats / critique:

  • 1.2 mM for breast is plausible. PMID 27100284 detected MICEST in breast cancer cell-line extracts, supporting detectability. However, typical brain myo-inositol is ~5-7 mM; the lower breast concentration is the primary reason contrast is ~30× below brain MICEST values.
  • Agree with six hydroxyl OH groups classed as 'hydroxyl.' The chemist's 1.0 ppm shift estimate is close to the simulated 0.725 ppm. However, the chemist calls the exchange regime 'fast' — at kex=600 s⁻¹, this is slow-to-intermediate at 7 T (Δω > k, per PMID 20951217), though it is fast at lower fields. This matters for sequence optimization.
  • PMID 20951217 reports in vivo human brain myo-inositol CEST peak at ~0.6 ppm from water. The simulated shift of 0.725 ppm is consistent. None — all six hydroxyl groups are accounted for. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor
  • Borderline case at ~1.2 mM. Six exchangeable -OH protons per molecule. CEST signal detectable at ~0.8–1.2 ppm offset at high field.

creatine — CEST: ✗ not detectable

Concentration: 1.00 mM typical (0.5–1.5)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Sitter 2006 quantified creatine in breast tissue at approximately 0.8–1.2 μmol/g depending on sample cellularity, corresponding roughly to 0.8–1.2 mM. The mean across all samples was ~1.0 μmol/g = ~1.0 mM. Creatine has an exchangeable guanidinium -NH2 group (~2.0 ppm) suitable for CEST (CrCEST). The concentration is borderline for the 1 mM threshold.

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (guanidinium NH2 [guanidinium]: concentration 0.5-1.5 mM, kex 80-1000 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.00-0.01%, 1.5 T: 0.01-0.03%, 3 T: 0.02-0.06%, 5 T: 0.02-0.09%, 7 T: 0.02-0.11%. Threshold 0.5%.

Frequency-collision analysis: At ≤5 T creatine (+2.00 ppm) blurs with β-glucose hydroxyls (+1.60 ppm): separation 8.5-85.2 Hz vs combined linewidth ~1054 Hz. At 7 T, separation is 119.2 Hz vs glucose linewidth ~1054 Hz — still overlapping. Creatine's own guanidinium linewidth (~218.8 Hz) is narrower than glucose's hydroxyl linewidth, so at 7 T partial resolution may be possible but not complete. Myo-inositol overlap resolves at ≥5 T. Semisolid MT resolves at 7 T.

Direct water saturation: At 0.5 T (B1=0.25 µT, bandwidth=10.6 Hz), the 2.0 ppm offset ≈ 42.5 Hz is outside the direct saturation band. At 1.5-7 T, the offset easily exceeds bandwidth (e.g., 7 T: 596 Hz offset vs 63.9 Hz bandwidth). Direct saturation is not a limiting factor for creatine.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex = 575 s⁻¹ is median of human muscle in vivo measurements (PMID 42249575: 150 s⁻¹; PMID 26374674: 1000 s⁻¹). No breast-specific measurement — borrowed from muscle. Exchange rate in breast may differ due to different pH and cellular environment. The 80-1000 s⁻¹ spread partially covers this, but muscle-derived rates may overestimate the true kex in acidic tumor tissue.

Caveats / critique:

  • 1.0 mM creatine for breast tissue is at the low end of plausible. Breast MRS typically reports tCr at ~1-3 mM; the 0.5-1.5 mM uncertainty range is reasonable. However, muscle CrCEST at ~30 mM produces strong contrast; the 20-30× lower concentration in breast is the dominant factor limiting detectability.
  • Fully agree with the guanidinium NH2 group at ~2.0 ppm classed as 'guanidinium.' This is the correct and well-known CrCEST pool. The chemist correctly identifies slow-to-intermediate exchange and calls this the best CEST candidate. No exchangeable protons were missed. PMID 37641066 successfully used MTRasym at 2.0 ppm in murine breast cancer, confirming the in vivo shift matches the reference-table value.
  • Highly consistent. None — the guanidinium NH2 is the only CEST-active pool; the N-methyl and carboxylate are not exchangeable. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Borderline at ~1 mM.
  • Creatine CEST (CrCEST) is established in muscle; its low concentration in breast may still produce detectable signal. Exchangeable guanidinium group.

Concentration: 1.50 mM typical (0.5–2.5)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Sitter et al. 2006 quantified β-glucose in breast tissue HR-MAS spectra, reporting ~1.5 μmol/g wet weight in non-involved tissue, which converts to ~1.6 mM. Sitter 2010 reported similar values. Breast tissue glucose is typically 0.5–2 mM depending on blood glucose and metabolic activity. Glucose has 4 exchangeable -OH groups per molecule (the β-anomer form measured) relevant for glucoCEST.

Robustness to input uncertainty: no

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (five hydroxyl OH groups (positions 1,2,3,4,6) [hydroxyl]: concentration 0.5-2.5 mM, kex 2400-14650 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.01-0.03%, 1.5 T: 0.01-0.04%, 3 T: 0.01-0.10%, 5 T: 0.01-0.17%, 7 T: 0.01-0.25%. Threshold 0.5%.

Frequency-collision analysis: At all fields (0.5-7 T), glucose (+1.60 ppm) overlaps with myo-inositol (+0.72 ppm): separation 18.6-260.8 Hz vs combined linewidth ~1058 Hz. Also overlaps creatine (+2.00 ppm): separation 8.5-119.2 Hz. These pools never resolve — glucose-weighted MTRasym at 1.2-2.0 ppm (PMID 37641066) includes contributions from myo-inositol and creatine. This is a major specificity issue.

Direct water saturation: At 0.5 T (B1=0.25 µT, bandwidth=10.6 Hz), the 1.6 ppm offset ≈ 34 Hz is ~3× the bandwidth — at the edge of direct saturation. At 7 T (B1=3.0 µT, bandwidth=127.7 Hz), 1.6 ppm = 476 Hz, so separation is adequate (3.7× bandwidth). The fast-exchange regime (kex=5850 s⁻¹) means the broad line itself, not direct saturation, is the limiting factor.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex = 5850 s⁻¹ is from phantom solutions (PMID 31313865, 20 mM glucose in PBS, pH 7.2, 37°C). Not from in vivo breast. Phosphate catalysis of hydroxyl exchange (PMID 32936483) means the in vivo kex may differ substantially (tissue phosphate is ~1-2 mM intracellular, much less than PBS). Temperature and pH in breast tumors also differ from the phantom conditions. The uncertainty spread 2400-14650 s⁻¹ partially covers this but the true in vivo value for breast is unknown.

Caveats / critique:

  • 1.5 mM endogenous glucose is reasonable for normoglycemic breast tissue. However, most glucoCEST studies use exogenous glucose injection raising tissue glucose to 5-20 mM. The simulation of endogenous levels is correct for baseline but does not reflect the typical experimental paradigm.
  • Agree with five hydroxyl OH groups classed as 'hydroxyl.' The chemist groups them into one pool, which is standard practice since individual hydroxyl shifts are close and exchange rates are fast, producing one broad envelope. The chemist correctly identifies the fast exchange regime. PMID 37641066 reports glucose-weighted CEST at 1.2-2.0 ppm in murine breast cancer.
  • The simulated shift of 1.6 ppm falls within this range, consistent with in vivo observations. None — the five hydroxyl groups are all exchangeable; the anomeric OH at position 1 is included. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor
  • Glucose is recognized as a CEST target (glucoCEST) via its hydroxyl protons. β-glucose is specifically reported by HR-MAS; total glucose (α+β) would be higher, approximately 1.7× the β value.

taurine — CEST: ? unknown (not simulated)

Concentration: 2.00 mM typical (1.0–3.5)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Sitter et al. 2006 (PMID 16229059) quantified taurine in breast tissue by HR-MAS 1H MRS and reported a mean concentration of approximately 1.6 μmol/g wet weight in breast cancer specimens, and similar or slightly lower values in adjacent non-involved tissue. Converting μmol/g wet weight to mM uses a density of ~1.04 g/mL and ~80% water content for breast parenchyma giving ~1.04–1.1 mmol/kg→mM; thus 1.6 μmol/g ≈ 1.7 mM wet tissue. This estimate is from cancer-adjacent tissue; values in normal premenopausal breast may be slightly higher because lactating/estrogen-stimulated breast accumulates taurine. The range 1.0–3.5 mM reflects inter-individual variation and the Sitter et al. data scatter; 2.0 mM is a reasonable single estimate. No direct human normal-breast-only study with molar concentrations was found, so this is an estimate.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — Sagittal oblique through the mid-breast (nipple line), aligned parallel to the chest wall

Why this scan: A single sagittal slice through the mid-breast captures three tissues with known large differences in metabolite concentrations: fibroglandular tissue (target, high myo-inositol, moderate glucose, low creatine), adipose tissue (high interstitial glucose, negligible creatine/myo-inositol), and pectoralis major muscle (very high creatine, negligible free glucose). If a Z-spectrum offset's contrast across ROIs tracks these known concentration gradients, it supports a real metabolite-specific CEST effect rather than a generic MT/NOE background that would appear uniform across tissues.

ROIWhere it is drawnRole
breast fibroglandular tissue target tissueCentral hyperintense glandular-stromal cone on the sagittal slice, avoiding visible fat lobules, the nipple, and the chest wall musculatureTarget tissue with intermediate creatine (1 mM), myo-inositol (1.2 mM), and glucose (1.5 mM)
breast adipose tissueSubcutaneous and retromammary fat compartments, drawn in regions clearly free of fibroglandular strands, anterior to the gland and posterior between gland and pectoralis fasciaComparison tissue with very low creatine (~0.1 mM), low myo-inositol (~0.1 mM), but high interstitial glucose (~3.5 mM)
pectoralis major muscleElliptical ROI drawn entirely within the pectoralis major belly posterior to the breast, avoiding ribs, intercostal muscles, and the skin lineComparison tissue with very high creatine (36 mM), very low free glucose (~0.3 mM), and intermediate myo-inositol (~0.5 mM)

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed rectangular train, B1=1 µT, 50 pulses × 20 ms (interpulse delay 10 ms, duty cycle 66.7%), total Tsat=1500 ms, TR=3000 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): At 3 T and 1.0 µT mean B1 with 66% duty cycle for 1.5 s, SAR in the breast (mostly adipose tissue, low conductivity) is well below IEC 60601-2-33 normal-mode limits for body coil. TR=3 s allows adequate recovery between shots. Similar protocols have been used for human breast glucoCEST without SAR violations.

Compromise rationale: B1=1.0 µT favours creatine guanidinium (optimal 1.0 µT at 3T) and moderately saturates myo-inositol hydroxyls (0.75 µT optimal) and glucose hydroxyls (1.5 µT optimal). Fast-exchange taurine and glycine amines (need >2 µT) are undersaturated and likely undetectable. The 66% duty cycle balances saturation efficiency against T1 recovery for the 3T breast water T1 (~1400 ms fibroglandular, ~250 ms adipose).

Fat suppression: SPAIR (Spectral Attenuated Inversion Recovery) with inversion time TI ~220 ms at 3 T to null fat signal before the saturation-readout train. Breast contains abundant adipose tissue; fat protons resonate at ~3.4 ppm, overlapping the amine CEST offsets (3.2 ppm taurine/glycine) and contaminating MTRasym analysis at all offsets due to the broad fat NOE at -3.4 ppm. SPAIR is standard in clinical breast MRI.

Motion mitigation: Voluntary end-expiration breath-hold (12-15 seconds per offset) with an abdominal pressure belt. Breast motion during free breathing is ~5-10 mm craniocaudal; a single-shot EPI readout per offset within a single breath-hold freezes this. The subject breathes freely between offsets (~5 s recovery). Total scan time for 23 offsets + WASSR is ~4-6 minutes, feasible for clinical volunteers.

Slice coverage: Single 8-mm thick sagittal oblique slice through the mid-breast at the nipple line, oriented parallel to the chest wall. FOV 180×180 mm, matrix 128×128, in-plane resolution 1.4×1.4 mm. The slice extends from the posterior pectoralis major to the anterior subcutaneous fat, capturing all three ROIs in one plane.

Structures in FOV: breast fibroglandular tissue, breast adipose tissue, pectoralis major muscle, skin, nipple

Z-spectrum sampling offsets:

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -5.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -3.50 ppm: NOE reference (fatty-acid NOE at -3.4 ppm), symmetric reference for MTRasym
  • -3.00 ppm: symmetric reference
  • -2.50 ppm: symmetric reference
  • -2.00 ppm: creatine reference (-2.0 ppm), symmetric reference for MTRasym
  • -1.50 ppm: symmetric reference
  • -1.00 ppm: myo-inositol/glucose hydroxyl reference (-1.0 ppm), symmetric reference for MTRasym
  • -0.80 ppm: symmetric reference for 0.8 ppm
  • -0.50 ppm: symmetric reference for 0.5 ppm
  • +0.00 ppm: water (saturation reference)
  • +0.50 ppm: myo-inositol hydroxyl (shoulder of envelope)

  • +1.00 ppm: glucose hydroxyl / myo-inositol hydroxyl envelope

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each metabolite's offset: (1) average Z-spectra per ROI, (2) compute MTRasym = Z(-Δω) - Z(+Δω), (3) test ROI differences via one-way ANOVA across voxels (p<0.05). For creatine at +2.0 ppm, pectoralis muscle should show 20-40x larger MTRasym than fibroglandular (36 mM vs 1 mM).
  • For the glucose/myo-inositol hydroxyl envelope (0.5-1.5 ppm), adipose should show higher MTRasym than fibroglandular if glucose dominates (3.5 vs 1.5 mM), but fibroglandular > adipose if myo-inositol dominates (1.2 vs 0.1 mM). A pattern where muscle>>fibroglandular~adipose at +2.0 ppm confirms CrCEST.
  • Lorentzian fitting separates the narrow guanidinium peak (creatine, ~1.5 ppm FWHM) from the broad hydroxyl envelope (glucose+myo-inositol, ~3-4 ppm FWHM). If all ROIs show identical MTRasym at a candidate offset after B0 correction, the signal is likely non-specific MT/NOE background.

Not actively targeted: Phosphocholine has zero exchangeable protons per the chemist agent (empty list); CEST detection is impossible. Taurine and glycine (fast-exchange amines at 3.2 ppm) are severely undersaturated at the compromise B1=1.0 µT (they need >2 µT for detectable contrast). Their offsets are sampled for completeness but detection is unlikely with this protocol. The scan design primarily targets creatine (2.0 ppm, slow exchange, 1.0 µT optimal) and the hydroxyl pool (myo-inositol + glucose at 0.5-1.5 ppm, partially saturated at 1.0 µT).

Caveats:

  • Partial-volume effects: the 8-mm slice unavoidably mixes fibroglandular tissue with fat strands, diluting concentration differences between ROIs. B0 inhomogeneity at breast air-tissue interfaces (skin, lung apex) causes off-resonance shifts up to 0.3 ppm even after WASSR correction, potentially mimicking or masking CEST effects at 0.5-1.0 ppm.
  • B1 inhomogeneity: body-coil transmission at 3T shows ±20% variation across the breast; the protocol resimulates at 0.7x and 1.3x B1 to test robustness. One compromise B1 (1.0 µT) cannot simultaneously optimize creatine (1.0 µT ideal), glucose (1.5 µT ideal), and fast amines (>2 µT ideal).
  • Breast adipose has short T2 (~50 ms) and a strong NOE asymmetry at -3.4 ppm that can spill into positive offsets if fat suppression is imperfect. The single-slice design sacrifices 3D coverage for acceptable scan time within breath-holds.
  • [Not simulated] No reference-backed simulation was possible for: breast fibroglandular tissue/taurine, breast fibroglandular tissue/glycine, breast fibroglandular tissue/phosphocholine, breast adipose tissue/taurine, breast adipose tissue/glycine, breast adipose tissue/phosphocholine, pectoralis major muscle/taurine, pectoralis major muscle/glycine, pectoralis major muscle/phosphocholine. Their predicted_contrast_percent is reported as 0 (not simulated), not as a prediction.
